- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, increase downward bias or add early correction to prevent overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 82.5), reduce forecast growth rate by 10–15% for next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 82.94 → 80.29 → 78.05), model should not continue upward trend beyond 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- Forecast should not exceed 83.5 unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.5) and recent history shows sustained upward momentum.  
- If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome drops sharply (e.g., 82.5 → 78.0), reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to account for sentiment decay.  
- Always check if forecast is trending above 83.0 with no recent negative sentiment — if so, flag for downward adjustment unless confirmed by macro or policy signals.
